title: Eviction-timing regression causing KV silt buildup and intermittent GPU OOM cascades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers (one Hosted high-throughput tenant, two Dedicated clusters, and a Private on-prem deployment) observed sudden GPU OOM cascades during short traffic surges over the last 72 hours. Symptoms were: long tail latency spikes, rapid session eviction churn, and eventual OOMs that required node restarts. Initial evidence pointed away from model size changes and towards memory allocator behavior combined with degraded KV cache compaction.

Root cause hypothesis: An eviction-timing regression introduced in runtime-1.24.0 changed the ordering of async eviction heartbeats and compaction windows. Under bursty traffic, small amounts of stale per-session KV state ('silt') accumulated because tombstones were not being compacted promptly. The allocator saw many small freed regions interleaved with pinned KV slabs, leading to fragmentation and inability to satisfy large transient allocations (batch peaks), causing GPU OOMs. The regression only appears under combined conditions: high concurrency + uneven key TTLs + older session sweeping heuristics (seen in Private deployments not on the latest housekeeping config).

Impact: Customer-facing timeouts (5-50s), increased error rates for generative requests, and manual node restarts for several Dedicated pools. One enterprise customer reported their inference throughput dropped 40% during the incident window and elevated support SLA.

Why this ticket: Track triage, fix, rollout, and postmortem actions. Deliver a targeted runtime patch that restores previous eviction ordering, adds a short-term aggressive compaction path for detected silt, and provides a telemetry signal for early detection.
acceptance_criteria: Patch landed that reorders eviction heartbeats to ensure compaction runs before low-priority eviction clears
Deployed hotfix to Hosted canary pool with no regression for 48h and no OOMs under synthetic surge test
Backport for Dedicated and Private customers with clear upgrade notes and a fallback flag
Instrumentation added: per-node silt_metric, compaction_latency, and fragmentation_ratio visible in Console
Post-deploy SLA check: impacted customer's latency and error-rate return to baseline within agreed window
steps_to_reproduce: Start runtime-1.24.0 with default compaction schedule on a 4xA100 node pool
Create 15 concurrent long-lived chat sessions with uneven prompt length distribution (10 short, 5 long) and TTLs staggered across 30-300s
Issue bursty parallel requests (3x normal QPS) for 90s to induce KV tombstone accumulation
Observe allocator fragmentation metrics and trigger synthetic allocation peaks (e.g., large batch inference) to reproduce OOM
Verify silt_metric and compaction_latency rise before OOMs
mitigation_steps: Immediate: increase eviction aggressiveness via runtime flag runtime.eviction.heartbeat_ms=1000 and force compaction window to 5s on affected pools
Hotfix: apply runtime-1.24.2 candidate that reorders compaction before low-priority evictions and adds an on-demand compaction API
Customer guidance: for Dedicated and Private, temporarily reduce per-tenant concurrency or enable quota-based throttling until patched
Rollback plan: if hotfix causes regressions, toggle runtime.eviction.legacy_order=true to revert behavior while investigation continues
rollout_plan: 1) CI: unit + integration tests for eviction ordering and compaction edge-cases
2) Nightly: run stress scenario (steps_to_reproduce) in staging for 6h
3) Canary: deploy to 10% of Hosted serving capacity during off-peak window, monitor silt_metric & OOMs for 24h
4) Gradual: expand to 50% then 100% Hosted if green; coordinate Dedicated customer upgrades with SEs; provide Private patch bundle and upgrade playbook
5) Post-rollout: monitor for 7 days and schedule a retro with ops and customer success
qa_plan: Automated fuzz test that simulates mixed TTLs and session churn validated against fragmentation_ratio threshold
Synthetic burst tests that emulate customer traffic profiles and assert no OOMs and latency < baseline *1.5
Chaos: scheduled pod restarts during canary to ensure graceful eviction and compact-on-recover behavior
Manual verification with impacted customer's traffic capture (redacted) in a sandbox
postmortem_actions: Finalize incident timeline and notify affected customers with root-cause explanation
Backfill missed metrics for silt_metric to enable earlier detection rules
Implement permanent invariant: ensure compaction runs at least once per X freed slab events
Add upgrade gating note for Private customers who skip housekeeping config changes
Schedule follow-up ticket to explore allocator redesign or slab coalescing (larger scope)
